description: Verify finishes before the first poll would fire, so the session emits zero wait turns and zero poll-loop growth. Identical under both profiles (there is no poll interval to change), so it is recorded once with profile "shared" rather than duplicated as baseline and proposed.
A typical one-minute verify polled at today's 10s cadence: 6 turns. The common case the current behavior is measured against.
The same one-minute verify at the proposed 180s cadence: a single turn. The common case the proposed behavior is measured against.

A 45-minute suite polled every 10s: 270 turns, each resending the whole conversation. This is the known-bad case that produced the 50-125M token production sessions. Not representative -- it is the pathology being reproduced, not an average input.
The same 45-minute suite at the proposed 180s cadence with a 15-turn cap: 15 turns. Representative of what a genuinely slow but healthy suite should cost under the proposed behavior.

A verify that never completes, polled every 10s until the 700-turn ceiling. WALLCLOCK_S is set to a 6-hour harness timeout so MAX_TURNS is the binding constraint rather than the wallclock. No task_complete is emitted. Not representative -- a worst-case ceiling check.
The same never-completing verify under the proposed 180s cadence and 30-turn cap. No task_complete is emitted. Not representative -- a ceiling check, not an average input.
